answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Consistency (CETC): each identity publishes a signed behavioural vector at every dawn; the next epoch must stay within a bounded divergence of the prior vector, checked against a rolling atlas of peer trajectories. A fresh identity starts with zero divergence history, so it cannot inherit trust, and splitting into N sybils forces N full histories plus per-epoch attestation costs, multiplying attacker overhead by N while detection horizon stays fixed.
